about: Idea cards for the design studio. Each seat is dealt three, from three different families, and answers its framings with them. A card is a forcing move: it pushes the seat away from the site anyone would make for this trade. The material cards start from what the business has; the idea cards turn what the business is into one governing idea; the constraint cards take something away; the visual cards start from light, space, material and mechanism, so what is left has to carry the design; the far fields are places outside the web to borrow from; the time cards are about movement and what it means; the voice cards make the words the design; the separation cards resolve one of the frame's contradictions. No card names a pattern of the web: a direction is not made by joining what other sites do.

cards.name: The thing itself
cards.prompt: Start from the product, the work or the place (an M… item) and let it be the whole first screen, at a size or from an angle nobody shows it.

cards.name: The process
cards.prompt: The business does something step by step that visitors never see. Make that making the structure of the site.

cards.name: The archive
cards.prompt: Something the business has kept for years (drawings, ledgers, samples, letters, old labels): build the look from it, not from stock.

cards.name: The numbers
cards.prompt: The business knows numbers about itself or its work (an M… or D… item). Let them be the imagery.

cards.name: The hands
cards.prompt: The people who do the work, their tools and their marks: let the site carry something made by hand by them.

cards.name: The place
cards.prompt: Where the business is: its light, its street, its weather, its materials. Take the palette and the rhythm from there.

cards.name: The by-product
cards.prompt: What the work leaves behind (offcuts, drafts, test pieces, crossed-out versions): make the leftover the ornament.

cards.name: The customer's own words
cards.prompt: Something customers say about the business, in their words, becomes the scene the site stages: what would a visitor see if that sentence were a place?

cards.name: The verb
cards.prompt: Say what the business does as one verb. Make the site do that verb to the visitor.

cards.name: The contradiction made visible
cards.prompt: Take one of the frame's contradictions and show both sides at once in the layout, instead of hiding one.

cards.name: The one object
cards.prompt: Choose one object that stands for the whole business. Everything on the site is arranged around it, or is it.

cards.name: The wrong scale
cards.prompt: Show the smallest thing the business cares about very large, or its largest thing very small.

cards.name: The rule
cards.prompt: Invent one strict rule the whole design obeys (everything travels left to right, nothing is a rectangle, light only comes from one side) that comes from how the business works.

cards.name: What it refuses
cards.prompt: Name the thing this business will not do that its rivals do. Let the design refuse something too, for the same reason.

cards.name: The visitor's question
cards.prompt: The one question every visitor arrives with. The site is the answer to it and nothing else until it is answered.

cards.name: One colour
cards.prompt: One colour and paper white. Which colour, taken from where in the business, and what does it have to do alone?

cards.name: One screen
cards.prompt: The whole site fits one screen with no scrolling. What stays, and how does a visitor reach the rest?

cards.name: No hero
cards.prompt: No large picture and headline at the top. What is the first thing a visitor meets instead, and why is it better?

cards.name: Half the words
cards.prompt: Half of everything the site says is cut. What is left, and what does the space it leaves become?

cards.name: Only what they have
cards.prompt: Nothing may be shown that the business does not already own or make: no stock, no generated pictures. Design from the M… items alone.

cards.name: How a poster does it
cards.prompt: One image, one line, read from across a street. What would this site be as a single poster, and what of that survives on a screen?

cards.name: How a film opens
cards.prompt: A title sequence sets the tone before the story starts. What would the first ten seconds be, and when should a visitor be able to skip them?

cards.name: How an exhibition does it
cards.prompt: Rooms, a route, one object lit in each, a label read up close. Borrow the way a good exhibition paces a visitor.

cards.name: How a building does it
cards.prompt: A threshold, a hall, light from one side, a stair that invites. Borrow the way a building brings someone in and lets them find their way.

cards.name: How a book does it
cards.prompt: A cover, a title page, margins, a running head, the turn of a page. Borrow one thing a well-made book does.

cards.name: How packaging does it
cards.prompt: What is said on the outside, what is found on opening, the pleasure of unwrapping. Borrow the order in which a good package reveals itself.

cards.name: How a map does it
cards.prompt: Everything at once and each thing in its place; a legend; detail on coming closer. Borrow how a map lets someone choose their own way.

cards.name: How a stage does it
cards.prompt: An empty stage, one light, an entrance. Borrow how a theatre makes a single thing matter by taking the rest away.

cards.name: How a shop window does it
cards.prompt: Seen in three seconds by someone walking past, changed with the season. Borrow how a window stops a passer-by.

cards.name: How a score does it
cards.prompt: Rhythm, rests, loud and soft, a theme that returns. Lay the page out as a piece of music is written.

cards.name: Cause and effect
cards.prompt: Nothing moves unless the visitor did something, and what moves is the answer to what they did.

cards.name: Weight
cards.prompt: Give things on the page weight: heavy things move slowly and settle, light things are quick. What in this business is heavy?

cards.name: The first second
cards.prompt: What is true of the site in its first second, before anything has loaded that can be waited for?

cards.name: The tenth visit
cards.prompt: Design for someone who has been here nine times and wants one thing. What do they see that a first visitor does not?

cards.name: The hour of the day
cards.prompt: The site is not the same in the morning and at night, in June and in December, because the business is not.

cards.name: The slow thing
cards.prompt: One thing on the site changes so slowly that a visitor notices only on coming back. What is it, and what does it say?

cards.name: The pause
cards.prompt: Put a deliberate pause where every other site hurries: before a price, after a claim, at the end. What fills it?

cards.name: The label
cards.prompt: Every button, heading and caption is written as this business would say it out loud. What do the plainest words on the page become?

cards.name: The list
cards.prompt: The site is a list: of works, of prices, of people, of days. Make the plainest form the most considered one.

cards.name: The footnote
cards.prompt: The small print, the aside, the correction in the margin: let what is usually hidden at the bottom carry the character.

cards.name: Separate in time
cards.prompt: Let both sides of the contradiction hold, at different moments of a visit: one on arrival, the other once the visitor has what they came for.

cards.name: Separate in space
cards.prompt: Let both sides hold in different places: one above the fold and the other below, one on a wide screen and the other on a narrow one.

cards.name: Separate on condition
cards.prompt: Let each side hold only for some visitors or some visits: the one who is new, the one who came back, the one who asked for less motion.

cards.name: Separate the part from the whole
cards.prompt: Let the whole have one quality and each part the opposite: calm as a whole, rich in each detail; loud at a glance, quiet up close.

cards.name: Light
cards.prompt: Where does the light come from in this business's world: a lamp, a screen, dawn, a furnace? Light the whole site from there, and let it change as the visitor moves.

cards.name: Depth
cards.prompt: The site is a space, not a sheet: things stand in front of and behind each other. What is near, what is far, and what does moving through it reveal?

cards.name: The material
cards.prompt: Everything on the page behaves like one material from the business's world (paper, cable, glass, water, metal): it folds, bends, catches light or flows as that material would.

cards.name: The mechanism
cards.prompt: Show the machine working: the parts, the connections, the moving pieces of how this business gets its work done, drawn so a visitor can watch it run.

cards.name: The camera
cards.prompt: The visitor is a camera moving through the business's world: a long take, a pull back to reveal, a close-up. Direct the shot.

cards.name: The diagram that lives
cards.prompt: The drawing the business would make on a whiteboard to explain itself becomes the site, and it comes alive under the visitor's hand.

cards.name: The transformation
cards.prompt: Something on the site turns into something else as the visitor scrolls: chaos into order, night into day, raw into finished. What turns into what, for this business?

cards.name: The answer to touch
cards.prompt: Every touch, click or pause of the visitor gets a physical answer: a ripple, a pull, a light that follows. What does this business's world do when touched?
